newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks trail Dow higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks trail Dow higher at open.

text.p: A buoyant Australian share market trailed stronger U.S. bond and equity markets higher at the open on Wednesday as traders took heart from well-received U.S. inflation data.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index jumped 15.6 points to 2,435.0.
"It was a very strong move on U.S. markets and things are looking very positive," said dealer at Daiwa Securities, Mark Pervan.
A weak gold price weighed on a generally upbeat resources sector, although heavier losses could have been expected given falls in the bullion price offshore.
"The golds seem to be performing pretty well. Some pundits may be thinking the gold price may be starting to bottom. Gold looks very cheap at the moment," Pervan said.
The upbeat tone taken early was expected to continue, although Pervan suggested some paring of gains later in the day could not be discounted.
"It looks very positive this morning but it may taper off a little in the afternoon," he said.
Early features on both sides of the ledger came from the miners.

The world's biggest zinc producer, Pasminco, shot ahead over eight percent to A$2.23 (US$1.74) early after the zinc price moved to 10-month highs in offshore markets and as investors factored in benefits from its planned Century zinc acquisition in North Queensland.
However, nickel producer QNI Ltd lost over four percent to A$2.58 in early trade following a first half profit downgrade, announced after the market closed on Tuesday.
Rises and falls were level pegging, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
